A critical value is a cutoff for a test statistic chosen so that the probability of falling in the rejection region under $H_0$ equals the significance level $\alpha$. Reject $H_0$ when the observed statistic lies beyond the cutoff in the direction specified by $H_a$.

A p-value is the probability, assuming $H_0$ is true, of observing a test statistic at least as extreme as the one obtained in the direction of $H_a$. Reject $H_0$ when the p-value is at most the chosen significance level $\alpha$.
